<!-- ======================================================================= -->
# Setup
<!-- ======================================================================= -->

The **Setup** chunk clears the workspace, loads the required packages, sets the session options, and reads the two pre-processed `.dta` files from `data/derived/` (the consistency-audit spreadsheet is read later, in its own chunk). Paths are resolved with the _here_ package, anchored to the project root via `here::i_am()`, so the working directory never has to be set manually.

```{r "setup", echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}

# clear workspace
rm(list = ls())

# load the required packages, pinned to the CRAN snapshot of `groundhog.day`
# so that every run uses the same package versions (requires R >= 4.6);
# knitr and rmarkdown come with the rendering front-end and stay unpinned
if (!require("groundhog", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("groundhog", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
  library(groundhog)
}
groundhog.day <- "2026-09-01"
packages <- c(
  "here", "haven",
  "labelled", "readxl", "stringr",
  "tidyverse"
)
groundhog.library(packages, groundhog.day)

# anchor here() to the project root, so paths resolve regardless of the
# working directory
here::i_am("code/01_data_processing.Rmd")

options(scipen = 6)    # discourage scientific notation

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo    = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE
)

# drop haven/labelled metadata so downstream pipes see plain vectors
strip_attrs <- function(x) { attributes(x) <- NULL; x }

data.derived <-
  read_dta(
    here("data", "derived", "ManyDaughters_preprocessed.dta")
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), strip_attrs))

data.idiosyncrasy <-
  read_dta(
    here("data", "derived", "idiosyncrasy_results_combined.dta")
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), strip_attrs))

rm(groundhog.day, packages, strip_attrs)

```



<!-- ======================================================================= -->
# Functions
<!-- ======================================================================= -->

Project-wide helpers. `select.mutate()` wraps `dplyr::mutate()` and keeps only the columns the mutation introduced or changed. `as.dummy()` turns the "Yes"/"No" strings returned by Qualtrics into a two-level (`no`/`yes`) factor; `as.treatment()` maps the 0/1 treatment code to a `control`/`data` factor; `yn()` builds a `no`/`yes` factor from a logical condition.

```{r "functions"}

# mutate, then keep only the newly created / modified columns
select.mutate <- function(.data, ...) {
  before <- names(.data)
  after  <- dplyr::mutate(.data, ...)
  dplyr::select(after, tidyselect::all_of(setdiff(names(after), before)))
}

# "Yes"/"No" string -> factor(no, yes)
as.dummy <- function(x) {
  factor(
    case_when(
      startsWith(x, "Yes") ~ 1,
      startsWith(x, "No")  ~ 0,
      TRUE                 ~ NA
    ),
    levels = c(0, 1),
    labels = c("no", "yes")
  )
}

# 0/1 treatment code -> factor(control, data)
as.treatment <- function(x) {
  factor(x, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("control", "data"))
}

# logical condition -> factor(no, yes)
yn <- function(cond) {
  factor(ifelse(cond, 1, 0), levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("no", "yes"))
}

```



<!-- ======================================================================= -->
# Data processing
<!-- ======================================================================= -->

The chunks below build one frame per facet of the project (entry survey, belief surveys, peer assessments, consistency audit, RT estimates, and team-level analysis variables). Each frame keeps only the analysis-relevant variables, renames them to shorter working names, and attaches variable labels.


## Entry survey
<!-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -->

The screening survey administered before randomization. `df.srvy` is in long format with one row per individual researcher and holds demographics, position, publication record, self-rated experience, and the recruitment channel, alongside team-level identifiers (team ID, size, treatment condition).

```{r "entry survey"}

# the ".m1" / ".m2" suffixes mark member-specific items (m1: lead respondent,
# m2: partner) and are pivoted into a long-format `member` column below
df.srvy <-
  data.derived %>%

  # completing research teams only (PAP §3)
  filter(PT_dropout == 0) %>%

  select.mutate(

    # team-level identifiers and treatment
    tid          = rt_id,
    pid.m1       = EC_pid,
    pid.m2       = EC_p_pid,
    size         = EC_rt_size,
    group        = as.treatment(EC_treatment),

    # recruitment channel (m1 / m2)
    recruit.m1   = ES_recruitment_channel,
    recruit.m2   = EC_p_recruitment_channel,

    # demographics (m1 / m2)
    lctn.m1      = ES_location,
    lctn.m2      = EC_p_location,
    gndr.m1      = ES_gender,
    gndr.m2      = EC_p_gender,
    field.m1     = ES_research_field,
    field.m2     = EC_p_research_field,
    career.m1    = ES_position,
    career.m2    = EC_p_position,

    # publications (m1 / m2)
    pub_top.m1   = as.dummy(ES_top_pub),
    pub_top.m2   = as.dummy(EC_p_top_pub),
    pub_emp.m1   = as.dummy(ES_empirical_publication),
    pub_emp.m2   = as.dummy(EC_p_empirical_publication),
    pub_rq.m1    = as.dummy(ES_study_daughters),
    pub_rq.m2    = as.dummy(EC_p_study_daughters),

    # self-rated experience (m1 / m2)
    exp_reg.m1   = as.numeric(ES_experience_regression),
    exp_reg.m2   = as.numeric(EC_p_experience_regression),
    exp_stata.m1 = as.numeric(ES_experience_stata),
    exp_stata.m2 = as.numeric(EC_p_experience_stata),
    exp_data.m1  = as.numeric(ES_experience_large_data),
    exp_data.m2  = as.numeric(EC_p_experience_large_data),
    exp_pap.m1   = as.numeric(ES_experience_pap),
    exp_pap.m2   = as.numeric(EC_p_experience_pap),
    exp_meta.m1  = as.dummy(ES_participated_metasci_study),
    exp_meta.m2  = as.dummy(EC_p_participated_metasci_study),
    exp_soep.m1  = as.dummy(ES_used_soep),
    exp_soep.m2  = as.dummy(EC_p_used_soep)
  ) %>%

  # reshape the m1 / m2 columns into a long-format `member` column
  pivot_longer(
    cols          = -c(tid, size, group),
    names_to      = c(".value", "member"),
    names_pattern = "(.*)\\.(m[12])"
  ) %>%

  # drop the empty m2 row for solo teams
  filter(!is.na(pid) & pid != "") %>%

  # collapse Qualtrics response strings into compact category labels
  mutate(
    recruit = case_when(
      startsWith(recruit, "Heard about")  ~ "Coordinators",
      startsWith(recruit, "Received")     ~ "Team member",
      startsWith(recruit, "Through Lab2") ~ "Lab² announcement",
      startsWith(recruit, "Through SOEP") ~ "SOEP announcement",
      startsWith(recruit, "Other")        ~ "Other",
      TRUE                                ~ NA_character_
    ),
    gndr = case_when(
      startsWith(gndr, "Other") ~ "Other",
      TRUE                      ~ gndr
    ),
    lctn = case_when(
      startsWith(lctn, "Central") ~ "Latin America",
      TRUE                        ~ lctn
    ),
    field = case_when(
      startsWith(field, "Business")   ~ "Business",
      startsWith(field, "Psychology") ~ "Psychology",
      startsWith(field, "Other")      ~ "Other",
      TRUE                            ~ field
    ),
    career = case_when(
      startsWith(career, "Other")    ~ "Other position",
      career == "PhD student"        ~ "PhD candidate",
      startsWith(career, "Bachelor") ~ "BSc or MSc student",
      TRUE                           ~ career
    )
  ) %>%

  arrange(tid, member) %>%

  set_variable_labels(.labels = list(
    tid       = "Research Team ID",
    pid       = "Participant ID",
    member    = "Team Member ID",
    size      = "Team Size",
    group     = "Treatment Condition",
    recruit   = "Recruitment Channel",
    lctn      = "Geographic Location",
    gndr      = "Gender",
    field     = "Research Field",
    career    = "Academic Position",
    pub_top   = "Top Publication",
    pub_emp   = "Empirical Publication",
    pub_rq    = "Study on Daughters Hypothesis",
    exp_reg   = "Experience: Regression (0-10)",
    exp_stata = "Experience: Stata (0-10)",
    exp_data  = "Experience: Large Data (0-10)",
    exp_pap   = "Experience: PAPs (0-10)",
    exp_meta  = "Experience: Meta-Science",
    exp_soep  = "Experience: SOEP"
  ))

```


## Belief surveys
<!-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -->

The prior beliefs elicited before Stage 1 (Survey #1) and the posterior beliefs elicited after Stage 2 (Survey #2). `df.blfs` is in long format with one row per (RT, hypothesis, stage); `belief` is each team's reported probability that the hypothesis is supported at the 5% level, rescaled from the elicited 0-100% to a 0-1 fraction.

```{r "belief surveys"}

df.blfs <-
  data.derived %>%
  filter(PT_dropout == 0) %>%

  select.mutate(

    tid          = rt_id,

    # Stage 1 priors (PAP §2.1, "Initial beliefs")
    belief.h1.s1 = as.numeric(BS1_prior_h1),
    belief.h2.s1 = as.numeric(BS1_prior_h2),
    belief.h3.s1 = as.numeric(BS1_prior_h3),
    belief.h4.s1 = as.numeric(BS1_prior_h4),

    # Stage 2 posteriors (PAP §2.1, "Beliefs after Stage 2")
    belief.h1.s2 = as.numeric(BS2_posterior_h1),
    belief.h2.s2 = as.numeric(BS2_posterior_h2),
    belief.h3.s2 = as.numeric(BS2_posterior_h3),
    belief.h4.s2 = as.numeric(BS2_posterior_h4)
  ) %>%

  # reshape h{1-4} × s{1,2} into long format
  pivot_longer(
    cols          = starts_with("belief"),
    names_to      = c(".value", "hyp", "stage"),
    names_pattern = "(.*)\\.([^.]+)\\.([^.]+)"
  ) %>%

  mutate(
    belief = belief / 100,    # rescale 0-100% to a 0-1 fraction
    hyp    = factor(hyp,   levels = c("h1", "h2", "h3", "h4")),
    stage  = factor(stage, levels = c("s1", "s2"))
  ) %>%

  arrange(tid, hyp, stage) %>%

  set_variable_labels(.labels = list(
    tid    = "Research Team ID",
    stage  = "Project Stage",
    hyp    = "RT Hypothesis ID",
    belief = "Belief: Support (0-1)"
  ))

```


## Peer assessments
<!-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -->

The peer-evaluation stage (PAP §1.7): each completing RT rated ten anonymized RT-PAPs (five per treatment group, excluding its own) on reasonableness and informativeness for each hypothesis. `df.evls` is in long format with one row per (rated team, hypothesis, rater); `group` is the rated team's treatment condition and the per-rating quality `qulty` is the mean of `rsnbl` and `infrm` (PAP §2.1).

```{r "peer assessments"}

# rated team -> treatment condition (the same completer-level mapping used by
# df.proc), attached so the rating regressions in 03 need no extra join
rated.group <-
  data.derived %>%
  filter(PT_dropout == 0) %>%
  distinct(tid = rt_id, group = as.treatment(EC_treatment))

# raw columns are wide:
#   PA_PAP{1..10}_h{1..4}_{reasonable,informative}  ratings the rater gave
#   PA_rated_rt_id{1..10}                            team rated in slot k
df.evls <-
  data.derived %>%
  filter(PT_dropout == 0) %>%

  # here rt_id identifies the rater (rid)
  rename(rid = rt_id) %>%

  # pivot all ratings (PAP slot, hypothesis, dimension) into long format
  pivot_longer(
    cols          = matches("^PA_PAP\\d+_h\\d+_(reasonable|informative)$"),
    names_pattern = "PA_(PAP\\d+)_h(\\d+)_(reasonable|informative)",
    names_to      = c("pap", "hyp", ".value")
  ) %>%

  mutate(pap = as.numeric(str_remove(pap, "PAP"))) %>%

  # look up the rated RT for this rater × PAP slot
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(tid = get(paste0("PA_rated_rt_id", pap))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%

  # numeric ratings + PAP §2.1 quality rating (mean of the two)
  mutate(
    rsnbl = as.numeric(reasonable),
    infrm = as.numeric(informative),
    qulty = (rsnbl + infrm) / 2,
    hyp   = factor(hyp, levels = 1:4, labels = c("h1", "h2", "h3", "h4"))
  ) %>%

  left_join(rated.group, by = "tid") %>%
  select(tid, hyp, rid, group, rsnbl, infrm, qulty) %>%
  arrange(tid, hyp, rid) %>%

  set_variable_labels(.labels = list(
    tid   = "Research Team ID",
    hyp   = "RT Hypothesis ID",
    rid   = "ID of Rating Team",
    group = "Treatment Condition",
    rsnbl = "Rating: Reasonableness (0-10)",
    infrm = "Rating: Informativeness (0-10)",
    qulty = "Rating: PAP Quality (0-10)"
  ))

rm(rated.group)

```


## Consistency checks
<!-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -->

The coordinators' audit of RT-PAP/code consistency (PAP §1.5). A random 10% of RT-PAPs was checked first; because the inconsistency rate exceeded the 20% escalation threshold, all pairs were subsequently reviewed. `df.cons` has one row per RT and records whether the team was in the initial 10% audit (`audit10`), the overall consistency verdict (`consistent`; PAP §2.1, 1 = consistent / 0 = inconsistent), and — for inconsistent pairs — the total number of inconsistencies (`n_incons`) and the count of each type. The 100%-sample file is read because it is a strict superset of the 10%-sample file, carrying the `10%_sample` flag and identical verdicts on the audited subset.

```{r "consistency checks"}

# the inc_* columns count inconsistencies of each type per RT (n_incons = sum)
df.cons <-
  read_excel(
    here("data", "derived",
         "PAPtoCode_ConsistencyCheck_100%sample_results.xlsx")
  ) %>%

  select.mutate(

    # IDs and treatment
    tid     = rt_id,
    group   = factor(case_when(
                startsWith(treatment_str, "data")    ~ "data",
                startsWith(treatment_str, "no-data") ~ "control",
                TRUE                                 ~ NA_character_
              ),
              levels = c("control", "data")),

    # part of the random 10% audit (PAP §1.5)
    audit10 = yn(`10%_sample` == 1),

    # PAP §2.1 RT-PAP-to-code consistency (1 = consistent, 0 = inconsistent)
    consistent = factor(as.integer(as.logical(is_consistent)),
                        levels = c(0, 1),
                        labels = c("inconsistent", "consistent")),

    # number and type of inconsistencies (full review)
    n_incons        = as.numeric(total_inconsistencies),
    inc_filter_less = as.numeric(`less_strict_filter_in_code`),
    inc_filter_more = as.numeric(`more_strict_filter in code`),
    inc_dv          = as.numeric(`different_dv_in_code`),
    inc_iv          = as.numeric(`different_iv_in_code`),
    inc_ctrl_less   = as.numeric(`less_controls_in_code`),
    inc_ctrl_more   = as.numeric(`more_controls_in_code`),
    inc_test        = as.numeric(`different_test_in_code`),
    inc_spec        = as.numeric(`different_specification_in_code`)
  ) %>%

  arrange(tid) %>%

  set_variable_labels(.labels = list(
    tid             = "Research Team ID",
    group           = "Treatment Condition",
    audit10         = "In Random 10% Audit",
    consistent      = "PAP-to-Code Consistency",
    n_incons        = "No. Inconsistencies",
    inc_filter_less = "Inconsistency: Less Strict Filter",
    inc_filter_more = "Inconsistency: More Strict Filter",
    inc_dv          = "Inconsistency: Different DV",
    inc_iv          = "Inconsistency: Different IV",
    inc_ctrl_less   = "Inconsistency: Fewer Controls",
    inc_ctrl_more   = "Inconsistency: More Controls",
    inc_test        = "Inconsistency: Different Test",
    inc_spec        = "Inconsistency: Different Specification"
  ))

```


## Research teams' estimates
<!-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -->

The team-level results from running each RT's analysis code on the 95% sample, plus the variables the preregistered analyses require and the outlier flags. The chunk produces:

- `z` — standardized effect size from the (logged) two-sided $p$-value, signed so that positive values indicate support for the hypothesis (PAP §1.8 / §2.1);
- `dir`, `sig`, `ssc` — direction, significance at $\alpha$ = 5%, and the joint "$p$ < 0.05 in the hypothesized direction" criterion (PAP §2.1);
- `abs_dev` — absolute deviation of `z` from the group × hypothesis mean (PAP §2.1);
- `outl_rsnbl` — low-reasonableness flag (average demeaned reasonableness rating below $-2 \times SD$; PAP §3.1.1);
- `outl_rsnbl_rt` — corrected low-reasonableness flag, with the SD taken over the RT-level average demeaned ratings rather than the individual demeaned ratings (**not preregistered**; documented in `03_preregistered_analyses.Rmd`);
- `outl_fences` — Tukey's-fences flag on `z`, per group × hypothesis (PAP §3.1.1);
- `indx` — per-(RT × hypothesis) idiosyncrasy index $I_{i,h} = 1 - F_{i,h}(D_5)$, with `n_plac` recording the number of placebo draws behind each cell (PAP §2.1).

See the pre-analysis plan ([osf.io/cny7d/](https://osf.io/cny7d/overview){.uri}) for full definitions.

```{r "RT estimates"}

df.rslts <-
  data.derived %>%

  # PAP §3 sample restrictions: completers only, excluding RTs whose
  # submitted results could not be reproduced
  filter(
    PT_dropout              == 0,
    RT_results_inconsistent == 0
  ) %>%

  # keep only the 95%-sample columns; *_5 holds the 5%-sample mirror and
  # *_manual the RT-supplied summaries (neither used here)
  select(
    rt_id, EC_treatment,
    starts_with("RT_h"),
    -ends_with("_5"),
    -ends_with("manual")
  ) %>%

  # reshape RT_h{1-4}_<field>95 to one row per RT × hypothesis
  pivot_longer(
    cols          = starts_with("RT_h"),
    names_to      = c("hypothesis", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "RT_(h[1-4])_(.*)95"
  ) %>%

  select.mutate(

    # IDs and treatment
    tid    = rt_id,
    group  = as.treatment(EC_treatment),
    hyp    = hypothesis,

    # raw estimates
    n_obs  = num_obs_,
    n_ind  = num_participants_,
    b      = as.numeric(coefficient_),
    se     = as.numeric(se_),
    fam    = family_,
    df_m   = model_df_,
    df_res = residual_df_,
    stat   = b / se,

    # log of the two-sided p-value, recovered analytically when the reported
    # value underflows to zero (only z- and t-cases underflow in our data)
    log_p = case_when(
      p_value_ == 0 & fam == "z" ~ as.numeric(
        log(2) + pnorm(-abs(stat), lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = TRUE)
      ),
      p_value_ == 0 & fam == "t" ~ as.numeric(
        log(2) + pt(-abs(stat), df_res, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = TRUE)
      ),
      TRUE ~ log(p_value_)
    ),

    # RT-supplied directionality of the test statistic relative to H_alt
    intprt = case_when(
      startsWith(interpretation_, "positive") ~ "positive >> support",
      startsWith(interpretation_, "negative") ~ "negative >> support",
      TRUE                                    ~ NA_character_
    ),

    # |z| from the (logged) two-sided p-value (PAP §1.8), signed so that
    # positive values indicate support for the hypothesis (PAP §2.1)
    abs_z = -qnorm(log_p - log(2), lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = TRUE),
    z = abs_z * case_when(
      intprt == "positive >> support" & b > 0 ~  1,
      intprt == "positive >> support" & b < 0 ~ -1,
      intprt == "negative >> support" & b < 0 ~  1,
      intprt == "negative >> support" & b > 0 ~ -1,
      TRUE                                    ~ NA_real_
    ),

    # direction, significance at α = 5%, and the PAP §2.1
    # "p < 0.05 in the hypothesized direction" criterion
    dir = factor(ifelse(z > 0, 1, 0),
                 levels = c(0, 1),
                 labels = c("negative", "positive")),
    sig = factor(ifelse(log_p < log(0.05), 1, 0),
                 levels = c(0, 1),
                 labels = c("p > 0.05", "p < 0.05")),
    ssc = yn(dir == "positive" & sig == "p < 0.05")
  ) %>%

  select(-abs_z) %>%

  # PAP §2.1 absolute deviation: |z - mean(z within group × hypothesis)|
  group_by(group, hyp) %>%
  mutate(abs_dev = abs(z - mean(z, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  ungroup()


# (i) low-reasonableness flags (PAP §3.1.1): average demeaned reasonableness
# rating below -2 × SD, where ratings are demeaned per rater × hypothesis.
# The registered rule (outl_rsnbl) takes the SD over the demeaned individual
# ratings per hypothesis; because RT-level averages are far less dispersed
# than individual ratings, that threshold binds for no team. The corrected
# rule (outl_rsnbl_rt) takes the SD over the RT-level average demeaned
# ratings instead -- a non-preregistered deviation, documented in the
# preamble of 03_preregistered_analyses.Rmd
evls.dm <-
  df.evls %>%
  group_by(rid, hyp) %>%
  mutate(rsnbl_dm = rsnbl - mean(rsnbl, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

df.rsnbl <-
  evls.dm %>%

  # average demeaned rating per RT × hypothesis
  group_by(tid, hyp) %>%
  summarise(rsnbl_avg = mean(rsnbl_dm, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%

  # per-hypothesis SD of the demeaned distribution (registered rule)
  left_join(
    evls.dm %>%
      group_by(hyp) %>%
      summarise(rsnbl_sd = sd(rsnbl_dm, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"),
    by = "hyp"
  ) %>%

  # per-hypothesis SD of the RT-level averages (corrected rule)
  group_by(hyp) %>%
  mutate(rsnbl_sd_rt = sd(rsnbl_avg, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%

  mutate(
    outl_rsnbl    = yn(rsnbl_avg < -2 * rsnbl_sd),
    outl_rsnbl_rt = yn(rsnbl_avg < -2 * rsnbl_sd_rt)
  ) %>%
  select(tid, hyp, outl_rsnbl, outl_rsnbl_rt)


# (ii) Tukey's-fences flag on z, per group × hypothesis (PAP §3.1.1)
df.fences <-
  df.rslts %>%
  group_by(group, hyp) %>%
  summarise(
    q1 = quantile(z, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3 = quantile(z, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  right_join(df.rslts, by = c("group", "hyp")) %>%
  mutate(outl_fences = yn(z < q1 - 3 * (q3 - q1) | z > q3 + 3 * (q3 - q1))) %>%
  select(tid, hyp, outl_fences)


# idiosyncrasy index (PAP §2.1): I_{i,h} = 1 - F_{i,h}(D_5), where F_{i,h} is
# the ECDF of p-values from RT i's code on placebo 5%-subsamples (iteration
# > 0) and D_5 is the original 5%-sample (iteration 0); the externally
# prepared file supplies the placebo draws.
#
# `distinct()` on the (RT, hypothesis, iteration) key guards against repeated
# iterations in the source file, which would otherwise enter the ECDF twice
# and weight those draws double. `n_plac` records how many placebo draws each
# cell actually rests on -- the target was 1,000, but not every cell reaches it.
df.indx <-
  data.idiosyncrasy %>%
  mutate(
    tid = rt_id,
    hyp = paste0("h", hypothesis)
  ) %>%
  select(tid, hyp, iteration, p_value) %>%
  filter(!is.na(p_value)) %>%
  distinct(tid, hyp, iteration, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  group_by(tid, hyp) %>%
  summarise(
    indx = {
      p_orig <- p_value[iteration == 0]
      p_plac <- p_value[iteration  > 0]
      if (length(p_orig) >= 1 && length(p_plac) >= 1) {
        1 - ecdf(p_plac)(p_orig[1])
      } else {
        NA_real_
      }
    },
    n_plac = sum(iteration > 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# merge the flags and the index into df.rslts
df.rslts <-
  df.rslts %>%
  left_join(df.rsnbl,  by = c("tid", "hyp")) %>%
  left_join(df.fences, by = c("tid", "hyp")) %>%
  left_join(df.indx,   by = c("tid", "hyp")) %>%

  set_variable_labels(.labels = list(
    tid           = "Research Team ID",
    group         = "Treatment Condition",
    hyp           = "RT Hypothesis ID",
    n_obs         = "No. Observations",
    n_ind         = "No. Individuals",
    b             = "Coefficient Estimate",
    se            = "Standard Error",
    fam           = "Test Family",
    df_m          = "Model DFs",
    df_res        = "Residual DFs",
    stat          = "Test Statistic",
    log_p         = "log(p-Value)",
    intprt        = "Interpretation",
    z             = "z-Value",
    dir           = "Directionality",
    sig           = "Significance",
    ssc           = "Stat. Sig. Criterion",
    abs_dev       = "Absolute Deviation",
    outl_rsnbl    = "Outlier: Low Reasonableness",
    outl_rsnbl_rt = "Outlier: Low Reasonableness (RT-Level SD)",
    outl_fences   = "Outlier: Tukey's Fences",
    indx          = "Idiosyncrasy Index",
    n_plac        = "Idiosyncrasy: No. Placebo Draws"
  ))

rm(evls.dm, df.rsnbl, df.fences, df.indx)

```


## Data preparation
<!-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -->

The team-level dependent variables (PAP §2.1) and the team-level independent variables used as controls (PAP §2.2), consolidated into one tidy frame `df.proc` with one row per RT. Together with `df.rslts` and `df.evls`, this frame is the basis for all preregistered analyses. See the pre-analysis plan ([osf.io/cny7d/](https://osf.io/cny7d/overview){.uri}) for full definitions.

```{r "data preparation"}

# team-reported dependent variables (PAP §2.1). The lit_search / smpl_anal /
# mltp_reg / effort items are stored as labelled response strings; the leading
# 0-10 numeral is extracted to recover the underlying score.
df.dv <-
  data.derived %>%
  filter(PT_dropout == 0) %>%

  mutate(across(
    c(BS2_lit_searched,
      BS2_simplest_analysis,
      BS2_effort,
      BS2_multi_regressions_considered),
    ~ as.numeric(str_extract(.x, "\\d+"))
  )) %>%

  select.mutate(

    tid         = rt_id,
    group       = as.treatment(EC_treatment),

    rprd_itrt   = PT_num_code_iterations,    # iterations to reproducibility
    effort      = as.numeric(BS2_effort),
    hours_spent = as.numeric(BS2_hours_spent),
    lit_search  = as.numeric(BS2_lit_searched),
    smpl_anal   = as.numeric(BS2_simplest_analysis),
    mltp_reg    = as.numeric(BS2_multi_regressions_considered)
  )


# team-aggregated independent variables (PAP §2.2): any-member dummies
# (seniority, economics, top_pub, exp_soep), member maxima of the experience
# scores, and team_of_two from team size
df.iv <-
  df.srvy %>%

  # member-level booleans / per-member averages
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    seniority = career %in% c("Full professor", "Associate professor"),
    economics = field  %in% c("Economics", "Finance"),
    exp_anal  = mean(c(exp_reg, exp_stata, exp_data), na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%

  # team-level rollup
  group_by(tid) %>%
  summarise(
    group       = factor(first(as.character(group)),
                         levels = levels(df.srvy$group)),
    team_of_two = factor(ifelse(first(size) == 2, 1, 0),
                         levels = c(0, 1),
                         labels = c("no", "yes")),
    seniority   = factor(ifelse(any(seniority), "senior", "junior"),
                         levels = c("junior", "senior")),
    economics   = factor(ifelse(any(economics), "yes", "no"),
                         levels = c("no", "yes")),
    top_pub     = factor(ifelse(any(pub_top  == "yes", na.rm = TRUE),
                                "yes", "no"),
                         levels = levels(df.srvy$pub_top)),
    exp_soep    = factor(ifelse(any(exp_soep == "yes", na.rm = TRUE),
                                "yes", "no"),
                         levels = levels(df.srvy$exp_soep)),
    exp_anal    = max(exp_anal, na.rm = TRUE),
    exp_pap     = max(exp_pap,  na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# RT-level idiosyncrasy index (PAP §2.1): mean of the four per-hypothesis
# indices, computed only for RTs with all four available
df.idxrt <-
  df.rslts %>%
  filter(!is.na(indx)) %>%
  group_by(tid) %>%
  summarise(
    indx_rt = if (n() == 4) mean(indx) else NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop"
  )


df.proc <-
  df.dv %>%
  left_join(df.iv,    by = c("tid", "group")) %>%
  left_join(df.idxrt, by = "tid") %>%

  set_variable_labels(.labels = list(
    tid         = "Research Team ID",
    group       = "Treatment Condition",
    rprd_itrt   = "Reprod.: No. Iterations",
    effort      = "Effort in Stages 1+2 (0-10)",
    hours_spent = "Hours Spent in Stages 1+2",
    lit_search  = "Literature Search (0-10)",
    smpl_anal   = "Simplest Analysis (0-10)",
    mltp_reg    = "Multiple Regressions (0-10)",
    team_of_two = "Team of Two",
    seniority   = "(Max.) Assoc./Full Prof.",
    economics   = "(Max.) Economist",
    top_pub     = "(Max.) AJG 4*/FT50 Pub.",
    exp_soep    = "(Max.) Experience: SOEP Data",
    exp_anal    = "(Max.) Experience: Analysis (0-10)",
    exp_pap     = "(Max.) Experience: PAPs (0-10)",
    indx_rt     = "RT Idiosyncrasy Index"
  ))

rm(df.dv, df.iv, df.idxrt)

```



<!-- ======================================================================= -->
# Export Environment
<!-- ======================================================================= -->

The **Export** chunk drops the helpers and the raw input data, then saves the remaining objects to `data/proc/_env.RData`, the image that the subsequent report files load. In addition, each processed data frame is written individually to `data/proc/` as both an `.rds` file (preserving column types and variable labels) and a `.csv` file (portable, human-readable).

```{r "export"}

# participant-flow counts, captured before the raw data is removed
# (PAP §3: report the number of RTs that drop out before completion)
df.flow <- tibble(
  recruited     = nrow(data.derived),
  dropout       = sum(data.derived$PT_dropout != 0, na.rm = TRUE),
  completed     = sum(data.derived$PT_dropout == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
  results_valid = sum(data.derived$PT_dropout == 0 &
                        data.derived$RT_results_inconsistent == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
) %>%
  set_variable_labels(.labels = list(
    recruited     = "Research Teams Recruited",
    dropout       = "Research Teams Dropped Out Before Completion",
    completed     = "Research Teams Completing All Stages",
    results_valid = "Completing RTs With Reproducible/Valid Results"
  ))

rm(as.dummy, as.treatment, yn, select.mutate)
rm(data.derived, data.idiosyncrasy)

# save(list = ls()) rather than save.image(): when the file is rendered into
# a separate environment (as run_all.R does), the frames do not live in
# .GlobalEnv and save.image() would write an empty file
save(list = ls(), file = here("data", "proc", "_env.RData"))

# per-frame copies: .rds keeps column types and labels, .csv is portable;
# runs after save() so the loop's scratch objects stay out of the image
for (nm in ls(pattern = "^df\\.")) {
  obj <- get(nm)
  saveRDS(obj,             here("data", "proc", paste0(nm, ".rds")))
  readr::write_csv(obj,    here("data", "proc", paste0(nm, ".csv")))
}
rm(nm, obj)

# write the Markdown codebook for the exported frames (see _codebook.R)
source(here("code", "_codebook.R"), local = TRUE)
write_codebook(here("data", "proc"))

```
